title: Performance Analysis of Runtime Handling of Zero-Copy for OpenMP Programs on MI300A APUs
problem: The penalty of data movement between host and device memory is a significant bottleneck for GPU applications. On MI300A APUs with unified memory architecture, it is unclear whether zero-copy memory access provides actual performance benefits compared to explicit copying, and what runtime overheads may occur.
motivation: Quantifying the performance characteristics of zero-copy on unified-memory APUs enables developers to make informed optimization decisions for HPC applications on MI300A systems.
method: The researchers added zero-copy support to OpenMP (a framework for parallel programming), which allows GPUs to read directly from unified memory (memory that both the CPU and GPU can access) without needing explicit data transfers. They tested this on MI300A APUs (AMD processors that combine CPU and GPU on one chip) using real production applications and SPECaccel 2023 benchmarks, comparing its performance against the traditional approach of copying data explicitly before GPU computation.
key_novelty: The authors measured zero-copy memory access on MI300A APUs and found its performance benefits vary significantly depending on the application type.
contributions: OpenMP runtime implementation enabling zero-copy memory access for MI300A APUs
Performance evaluation showing 1.2X-2.3X speedup for production applications over explicit copying
Characterization of zero-copy overhead revealing up to 11% performance penalty for certain benchmarks
Developer guidance on memory access optimization trade-offs for unified-memory systems

metrics.speedup: 1.2X-2.3X for production applications; up to 11% penalty for SPECaccel benchmarks

primary_theme: zero-copy memory optimization on unified-memory APUs
